title: always/usually/often etc. (word order 2)
subtitle: I always drink coffee.
summary: Put always, usually, often, never etc. before the main verb, but after am/is/are and between two verbs.

lesson.heading: Words in the middle
lesson.text: Words like **always** and **never** go with the verb in the middle of the sentence. They do not go at the beginning and they do not go at the end.

examples.text: *A:* Don't forget to phone Laura. *B:* I**'ve already phoned** her.

lesson.heading: These words go in the middle
Before the verb, but after am/is/are

left.label: before the main verb
left.text: always, often, never etc. come before go, play, have, drink, watch ...
examples: I **always drink** coffee in the morning.

right.label: after am/is/are/was/were
right.text: But they come after am, is, are, was and were.
examples: They **are never** at home during the day.
It **is usually** very cold here in winter.
When I was a child, I **was often** late for school.
*A:* Where's Laura? *B:* She**'s still** in bed.
I've got two brothers. They**'re both** doctors.

lesson.note: We say *I am always tired*, not ~~I always am tired~~. But *I always drink coffee*, not ~~I drink always coffee~~.

lesson.heading: Between two verbs
lesson.text: When there are two verbs (**will** ... **remember**, **can** ... **find**, **have** ... **been**), the word goes between them.

examples.text: **Do** you **usually go** to work by car?
My friends **have all gone** to the cinema.

lesson.text: Never put these words between the verb and the object: *He also plays tennis*, not ~~He plays also tennis~~.

exercises.prompt: Paul says he plays tennis often. Write a sentence about him.
exercises.explanation: often comes before the main verb plays.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Do you get up early? *B:* Yes, always. -> He ___ up early.
exercises.explanation: always comes before the main verb: He always gets up early.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Are you ever late for work? *B:* No, never. -> He ___ late for work.
exercises.explanation: never comes after is: He is never late for work.

exercises.prompt: Does always come before or after these words?
Write the sentence 'Susan is polite' with always.
Write 'I finish work at 5 o'clock' with usually.
options: I usually finish work at 5 o'clock.
I finish usually work at 5 o'clock.
I finish work usually at 5 o'clock.
exercises.explanation: usually comes before the main verb finish.
The word comes after isn't: The bus isn't usually late.
With two verbs (don't ... eat), often goes between them.

exercises.statement: Jane doesn't usually work on Saturdays.
exercises.explanation: Correct. usually goes between doesn't and work.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Do you speak Italian? *B:* Yes, and I ___ French.
exercises.explanation: also comes before the main verb speak, not after the object.

exercises.statement: I can remember never his name.
exercises.explanation: I can never remember his name. never goes between the two verbs.

exercises.prompt: Ask if Tina is here, using already.
